final_trade_decision:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: **AMZN — Overweight (staged accumulation, not a single-entry Buy).** The business case is decided by the fundamentals (four quarters of accelerating revenue to 13.9%, operating income roughly tripled to $36.9B, record 6.4% operating and 47.0% gross margins, FCF swung ~+$49B to +$32.2B at 1.06x net income, current ratio repaired 0.94x → 1.05x), while the bear's case is purely an entry-timing objection at a 2024 closing high of 180.38. Act in three tranches: a 25% starter near 180.38, the preferred 40% add on a pullback into the 177.10–178.35 VWMA/10-EMA confluence (extending to 176.82 and 173.30–173.52), and a conditional 35% only on a daily close above 181.70 with volume ≥45M and the MACD histogram positive. Size the aggregate so a slide from average cost to the 171.47 close-based stop costs ≤1.5% of portfolio value; 165.74 is thesis-level invalidation. If the account already holds AMZN, hold the core and skip the starter.

**Investment Thesis**: **What decided the direction: the fundamental inflection, which the bear conceded.** Revenue accelerated for four consecutive quarters (9.4% → 10.8% → 12.6% → 13.9%) on a ~$575B base, operating income roughly tripled ($12.2B → $36.9B), operating margin hit a record 6.4% above the 2020 peak, gross margin a record 47.0%, and FCF swung from –$16.9B to +$32.2B (~+$49B) with FCF/net income at 1.06x — cash-backed earnings power, not an accrual story. The balance sheet genuinely repaired: current ratio 0.94x → 1.05x, cash +36% to $73.4B, liabilities/equity 2.17x → 1.61x. The bear's own words — "the 10-K is real… I accept the data" — conceded the business and retreated to "quality is not valuation." That retreat does not hold up as a rejection, because no valuation multiple (market cap, P/E, EV/EBITDA) is available to either side: the gap is symmetric, so neither "already in the price" nor "temporarily unloved" can be proven. The bear also conceded it would flip on a confirmed breakout, which makes its position a timing call, not a deterioration thesis.

**What decided the execution: the bear's real point is asymmetry at the range top.** At 180.38 AMZN sits at a new 2024 closing high, +23.9% above the 200 SMA and +5.8% above the 50 SMA, with only ~1.3% to the 181.70 ceiling versus 3–5% to meaningful support. The 3/28 high pierced the upper Bollinger band (181.70 vs 181.51) and closed back inside; March volume ran ~36M against 45–50M+ in February; MACD remains in a bearish cross (2.547 vs 2.599, histogram –0.053); RSI 61.90 versus February peaks of 73.78/72.43 is a mild negative divergence; and with ATR at 3.26 an ordinary session can cut the 10 EMA (178.35) and VWMA (177.10). Macro is a near-term multiple headwind: 10Y at 4.20% (March high ~4.34%), CPI +3.09%, Fed on hold 7+ months, Mag 7 rotation, gold at highs, sentiment Neutral 5.1 on only one of three sources.

**Why that governs execution and not direction.** The primary trend is confirmed — price above a rising 10/50/200 stack (180.38 > 178.35 > 170.51 > 145.58), ascending March lows 171.47 → 179.26, price above a rising VWMA of 177.10. So we get long gradually and let the market come to the pullback confluence, paying up only on a breakout validated by volume ≥45M and a positive MACD histogram. A breakout without that volume signature is the bear's failed-breakout scenario. Structural stops, never inside the 179.3–180.2 noise band: close-based stop below 171.47 (~2.7 ATR, ~4.9% below entry) on starter and breakout tranches; 165.74 is thesis-level invalidation for the whole position.

**Sequencing risks I am underwriting rather than ignoring:** ~87% of FY2023 FCF landed in Q4, so Q1–Q3'24 FCF prints will look poor against the run-rate — a weak FCF headline alone is expected seasonality and is not a sell signal; the capex cut (–17.2% to $52.7B) is the exhaustible half of the FCF story; 400bps of margin expansion in one year is not repeatable; and H2'24 laps 7.8% operating-margin comps.

**What would change the call:** (a) failed breakout — rejection at 181.70 on volume ≥45M closing back below 177.10; (b) 10Y decisively above 4.34%; (c) a weak Q1'24 FCF print *coupled with* commentary implying the Q4 concentration was not seasonal; (d) arrival of actual valuation data showing a clear premium to AMZN's own history without matching earnings revisions. Partials into 186–188 on the measured move from the 165.74–181.70 range.

**Explicit information gaps:** no valuation multiples, no insider-transaction data, no AWS or advertising segment detail, and an incomplete (1-of-3 source) sentiment read. Any of these could change sizing; narratives that depend on them should be down-weighted. Note also that no risk-management debate was conducted on this proposal, so the sizing and stop discipline above are mine and must be applied by the caller rather than assumed enforced.

**Price Target**: 197.7

**Time Horizon**: 6-12 months (partial scale-outs into 186-188 within 1-3 months)
